title: How Dancing Transforms Your Brain
description: Luyện nghe bài học IELTS Listening chuyên sâu về tác động thần kinh của việc nhảy múa đối với não bộ, trí nhớ và sự suy giảm nhận thức khi về già.
transcript:
There are ways to make your brain bigger, faster, and stronger, and dancing is one of the best. It doesn't just use your whole body, but works most of your brain too. A bit like jogging and doing a Sudoku at the same time. Here are four ways dancing transforms your brain and makes it more ___resilient___.

Dancing lights up the whole brain. These are the parts you use when you balance and ___coordinate___ your movements. When you see others dance around you and work out where your body is in the space, as well as learning and remembering a routine, being ready to react, especially if anything goes wrong. And maybe the hardest part, staying motivated to keep dancing week after week. All of this activity means it can be better for the brain than other types of exercise. Doctor Chen is a former professional dancer and explains why.

If we are just exercising our muscles, for example, if we're just running on the treadmill or if we're just lifting weight, over time, that just becomes ___muscle___ memory and you're not so much challenging your brain anymore. Whereas dancing, you're constantly engaging different parts of the brain. Like doing a workout to shape your body, you can also shape your brain. It has an extraordinary ability to grow, rewire, and reorganize your whole life. This is called ___neuroplasticity___, and dance is good brain exercise.

So when you dance, research has shown that it grows the ___gray___ matter, and it grows the ___white___ matter as well, and make these ___pathways___ more efficient and make your ___neurons___ bigger and make them more effective.

Let's break it down. The brain is formed of cells called neurons. That's what brain tissue is made of. Each neuron has a head, which is its control center. Together they make up the gray matter in the outer layer of the brain. This is where information is received and processed. The tail of the neuron, or ___axon___, is the white matter. It's the central connective tissue and sends messages around the different brain regions and the rest of the body. So dancing can actually increase all that brain tissue.

And scientists have also found that regular exercise makes the brain stronger by producing more of an incredibly helpful substance. When you dance or when you exercise in general, you produce this hormone called ___brain-derived___ neurotrophic factor. And it's basically a ___fertiliser___ for your brain cells. And it helps your brain cells grow. And it helps with neuroplasticity.

The human brain is made up of about 86 billion of these cells. Each neuron can fire between one and 200 times per second, depending on what you're doing. These neural messages are ___electrical___ pulses sent back and forth faster than the blink of an eye and dance has been shown to improve the way these messages travel. This is something Doctor Julia Basso sees when she measures the brain activity of dancers using specialized caps as they move in real time. She's the dancer on the left.

The flow of information from one region to another can be faster, and it enhances our ability to learn and remember information, to have better ___cognitive___ function and to support emotional health. Because your brain controls your body. If your neurons communicate better, that can impact nearly everything you do. So ___coordination___ is going to be improved. The way we respond to others through ___communication___ and through speaking is going to be improved. The way we may even answer math questions or other ___problem-solving___ abilities will be enhanced.

Whether in a class a club on TikTok or when no one is watching, dancing feels good. This is because the brain releases an enjoyable cocktail of ___hormones___ that boost your mood. They're the ones you've probably heard of, like ___endorphins___, the body's natural painkiller, ___dopamine___, and ___serotonin___, both natural mood lifters. And if you're dancing with other people, you also get ___oxytocin___, the bonding hormone.

The more you do an activity like dancing, the more your brain looks forward to even craves doing it again. The more we participate in dance, and the more it's exposed to these neurochemicals, the more you're going to want to have those experiences and feel those sensations. And this is one of the reasons why people keep coming back to the dance floor.

While you might not notice the impact of your bigger, faster brain now, it could be extremely important as you get older. As we age, our neurons naturally start to die. This can lead to ___degenerative___ diseases like Parkinson's and Alzheimer's. There is no cure for these illnesses, only prevention. The best way to do that. Build up a big ___neural___ reserve. You can think of it as like a savings account and activities like learning or, really complex work or dancing are like making deposits into your savings bank. A catastrophe happens if you only have $100, you're going to go into debt. But if you have $1 million, for example, if you have a good ___cognitive___ reserve, you have a lot of money. Having lots of neurons means you have many potential ___routes___ for messages to travel, not just one or two. So then you can ___bypass___ the neurons that have died with other ___alternative___ pathways that maybe other people don't have. But you have because of what you built over the years.

There's scientific evidence that dance helps do just that. Researchers looked at links between different ___leisure___ activities and the risk of ___dementia___. The study followed the impact of 11 physical exercises like swimming, walking or doing housework. Dancing was the only one shown to lower the risk of dementia. When we age, the brain starts to ___degenerate___, and dance can help stave that off. It can help to increase cognitive function, support brain health in general, grow neurons, and increase neurotransmitters that may be declining during the aging process. Now, that being said, starting dance at any age will be beneficial because neuroplasticity happens throughout the entire ___lifespan___.

mcqQuestions.q: What does the speaker mean by comparing dancing to 'jogging and doing a Sudoku at the same time'?
options: Dancing requires equal physical exertion as running marathon distances.
Dancing uniquely combines heavy physical effort with complex mental stimulation.
Playing Sudoku while running is recommended for brain development.
Jogging helps you solve puzzles faster.

mcqQuestions.q: Why does running on a treadmill become less challenging for the brain over time?
options: Running on a treadmill causes long-term muscle damage.
Repetitive exercise becomes muscle memory and requires less active brain engagement.
Treadmills are ineffective for physical fitness.
Muscle memory prevents the brain from remembering new information.

mcqQuestions.q: What is the key idea behind 'Like doing a workout to shape your body, you can also shape your brain'?
options: Physical exercise alters the physical shape of your skull.
Body workouts directly increase your IQ score.
Brain shaping requires surgical procedures.
Brain structure can be changed and strengthened through targeted cognitive and physical activity.

mcqQuestions.q: What is the function of Brain-derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) when described as 'a fertiliser for your brain cells'?
options: BDNF is a chemical used in agricultural testing.
BDNF promotes the growth, nourishment, and connection of neurons.
Fertiliser can be directly applied to treat brain injuries.
BDNF causes brain cells to divide uncontrollably.

mcqQuestions.q: What does the phrase 'electrical pulses sent back and forth faster than the blink of an eye' illustrate?
options: Looking away prevents neural signals from reaching the brain.
Blinking helps brain signals travel at higher speeds.
Neural communication within the brain occurs at an extremely high speed.
Electrical shocks can enhance memory formation.

mcqQuestions.q: How does enhanced neural communication impact daily performance?
options: It speeds up data processing across brain regions, improving learning, memory, and coordination.
It helps dancers learn foreign languages faster than non-dancers.
Memory retention depends solely on information processing speed.
Moving quickly improves overall test performance automatically.

mcqQuestions.q: What causes the positive mood elevation when people dance?
options: Drinking alcohol while dancing enhances mood regulation.
The brain releases a rich cocktail of hormones like endorphins, dopamine, and serotonin.
Mood boosters are synthesized artificially inside the brain.
Hormones function similarly to chemical cocktails.

mcqQuestions.q: Why do people keep coming back to the dance floor according to the transcript?
options: Dancing leads to dangerous addiction patterns.
Exposure to neurochemicals creates positive sensations that the brain craves repeatedly.
Brain cravings only occur during physical exhaustion.
Craving dance reduces motivation for other daily tasks.

mcqQuestions.q: What is the purpose of building up a 'cognitive reserve' or 'neural reserve'?
options: Brain health requires saving money for medical care.
Accumulating alternative neural pathways protects against cognitive decline and brain damage in old age.
Savings accounts prevent neurological diseases.
Neurons can be saved and spent like currency.

mcqQuestions.q: What unique finding did researchers discover regarding leisure activities and dementia risk?
options: Non-dancing exercises provide no health benefits.
Dancing was the only physical leisure activity among 11 studied that significantly lowered dementia risk.
Dementia can be cured entirely through dance therapy.
Other leisure activities increase dementia risk.
